key_insight: A multi-agent healthcare framework uses deterministic safety gates to prevent premature diagnostic handoff and reduce silent hallucinations by requiring complete symptom capture and checking output uncertainty.
clinical_relevance: This could improve the reliability of AI-assisted triage and diagnostic support by making the system wait for structured symptom data before moving to conclusions.
method: Uses a neuro-symbolic state tracker to enforce OLDCARTS completeness.
Blocks diagnostic transitions until all required symptom dimensions are collected.
Applies semantic entropy from 5 sampled outputs to flag divergent or uncertain responses.
evidence_signal: In 150 simulated test cases, the full system reached 49.3% diagnostic precision, an 11.3-point gain over the unconstrained baseline, with OLDCARTS completeness negatively correlated with semantic entropy (r = -0.181, p < 0.05).
watch_item: Results come from simulated patient interactions rather than real clinical deployment, so generalizability, workflow fit, and safety in live settings still need validation.
paper_title: Agentic AI-based Framework for Mitigating Premature Diagnostic Handoff and Silent Hallucination in Healthcare Applications
